pairs.subject: client-fetch-cache
pairs.evidence: features/votetrack/getKompas.ts:61 The kompas read is one request-scoped React cache() flight that reuses the shared memoized vote record rather than keeping its own memo, and the client tree's only cache is a useMemo over the pure scoreAlignment derivation; no technique is realized the way the standard names as a failure.

techniques.evidence: features/votetrack/getKompas.ts:61 React cache() memoizes the promise per request at the loader layer, so every caller in one render joins one flight. The body catches and returns null, so a failure reaches all joiners as the same null. This is server-side and has only one caller today (app/kompas/page.tsx:33).

features/votetrack/getKompas.ts:68 The shared vote-record read is one plain module-level function (getVoteRecord.ts) that both /hlasovani and /kompas call, rather than kompas re-typing its own fetcher and derivation (the header comment records that it did this until 2026-08-11).

features/votetrack/getKompas.ts:19 Kompas makes no lifetime claim of its own on the shared record entry, which avoids two clocks over one entry. KompasPage.tsx:30 imports the shared MONEY_MEMO_TTL_MS rather than redeclaring it.

features/votetrack/kompas/KompasPage.tsx:38 A single-slot useMemo over a pure derivation, which stays the one way to compute the result. It is keyed by reference identity, and that is sound because the producer always mints a new Map (useKompasAnswers.ts:58 `const next = new Map(answers);`) and data is an immutable server prop. The technique also asks for that assumption to be written at the cache; that comment is missing.

features/votetrack/kompas/KompasPage.tsx:39 The memo key covers every input to scoreAlignment, with no hidden ambient axis. getKompas takes no arguments, so its cache() key is complete by construction.
features/votetrack/kompas/KompasPage.tsx:32 The client tree gets its data as server-rendered props and fetches nothing, so there is no client-fetched result to keep past an unmount.
